title: Refreeze candidate after Linux Vulkan repairs
requires: Green protected CI and complete physical Linux Vulkan installed-public evidence for the repaired candidate closure
scope: Freeze a new immutable sole-path candidate only after F8-66 repairs and physically proves the Linux Vulkan Gallery, installed-public, scenario and workload paths. Record one exact source commit, tree, candidate binary/deployment identity, manifest hash, complete protected closure, runtime variants, toolchains and green exact-source CI run. Preserve candidate v7, its passing F8-24 Linux CUDA evidence and failing F8-25 Linux Vulkan evidence as historical provenance; never union their observations with the replacement. Route F8-25 through F8-30 and F8-53 to the replacement through a separate coordination change, and create F8-68 for replacement-candidate Linux CUDA requalification, before any qualification row becomes ready.
acceptance: A new immutable candidate manifest records the exact repaired source commit/tree, public headers, shared Slang sources, runtime variants, all 49 capability rows and 30 public cases, cases/goldens, executable capture producer, fixture/validator contract, fixed budgets and unchanged quality tolerances.

The protected closure is mechanically regenerated and independently hash-verified. Exact-source protected CI, the complete required physical Linux Vulkan suite, pinned SPIR-V validation, installed SDK relocation, Gallery regression, public cases, scenario capture and desktop workload budgets pass from the frozen source and named binaries.

Candidate v7, manifest SHA-256 15f168583cdd16afbf0fa3d7a26a86349dab206e6aab87e9b3f1b18bdcbb8b8f, F8-24 pass evidence and F8-25 failure evidence remain byte-immutable historical provenance; no old pass is relabeled or combined with replacement evidence.

A coordination-only change writes the replacement candidate id, manifest hash, source/tree, exact CI run and failure provenance into F8-25 through F8-30 and F8-53, and adds F8-68 as a new Linux CUDA requalification follow-up preserving F8-24 as completed history, before any device task becomes ready.

Every device can reproduce the replacement capture from documented installed-public commands without changing physics, capabilities, cases, work budgets, tolerances, required timeouts or schedule. Any later protected change creates another candidate rather than mutating this freeze.
